item.content:encoded: Hello everyone, I go by the username yitsu. I first discovered the SCP Foundation on YouTube and was instantly hooked. I would watch any other SCP videos that would show up on my YouTube page. Eventually, I wondered where the information about these SCP's was shared and found out about the SCP Foundation Wiki page. There were so many SCP's than I originally thought there were. I am interested in writing my own SCP's for the foundation. I just really enjoy reading about different unique SCP's and also interested in writing some of my own.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hey DashDotBlank, and welcome to the site! Always great to welcome a long time fan to the ranks of members here. I like your attitude towards all this, and it's definitely a process to get an idea critiqued and reviewed before being able to even get to the drafting phase. With those kind of themes, I think youll fit in just fine. As well as good taste in games, enjoy the gaming. Take your time and get acquainted with how everything here works, and make sure to check out IRC chat too!

For my recommendation, you should check out SCP-5545

+ Resources
- Hide Resources

For posting ideas, make sure you go through the proper greenlighting process on the idea forums first. Remember that there is no rush, and you should take time familiarizing yourself with how Series 6 articles are formatted. We are a rather unique bunch so I'm sure just reading and being a part of the community will be rather fun for you!

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.


Best of luck!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hello,

my pen name is Galvaude and I'm really looking into participating in this awesome community. I discovered the SCP Foundation through the "Infographic Show" short's. The video of SCP-1981 really made me want to dig more into the SCP universe and here I am!

I've always liked horror-ish stories with mind-breaking technology and moral twisting entities ; from Poe to Warhammer 40k. I am here to contribute to the SPC universe with, I hope, interesting content for the readers/community to enjoy. I have studied political science, more specificaly political philosohpy, and I believe this will show in my future SPC stories. I also really enjoy discussing ideas and concepts, so I'm willing to engage in any on-going discussions! English is not my first langage, although I had to learn it at a young age. My first langage is french (Canada).

As for my hobbies, I DM, I play videogames (mostly RPGs - Big fan of the Baldur's Gate saga), and write poetry, short stories, make experimental videos, etc… my hobbies are always artistic but with a situationnist touch (check out what is situationnism). This is one of the reason I joined this community ; I feel like the collective approach is definitly situationnist in it's nature (being collective and anonymous). I like it alot!

As for the SCP, I am definitly intrigued (more and more) about the Thaumiel class. I have read all the SCPs that are listed under this class and I am fascinated by the boundary between the Keter and Thaumiel class (like SCP-1968). I think I'm going to dig deeper into that relation and on how the foundation deals with that. If anyone would be kind enough to guide me through existing conflictual/boundary-crossing SPCs and potential debates on classes, that would be really nice :). Of course, this is not to proove that the S/E/K/T(N) system does not work, it is just that I like to swim in uncharted waters.

I am definitly looking into making SCP articles, and I really appreciate the peer-reviewed system that is established here.

As per the december question, I think my answer relates to the colours you see when you close your eyes. I always wonder if I can control them or not, and if I could control them, would the patterns be as pretty? And then I fall asleep lol

Cheers and Merry Christmas lol
-Galvaude

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded: Hi, I’m Graxonus. I found out about SCP via Containment breach, and then started to dig deeper into the Foundation’s lore. Fairly soon, I discovered the site, and I loved it. So then I thought, “why not join it?” And so I did. I joined in explorer primarily because I want to mostly do feedback and things like that, and then contribute when I feel the article is good enough or I have enough free time to draft one up. My hobbies are reading, studying history, video games and swimming. I particularly love swimming, even though I am ironically allergic to salt water, meaning I can never really swim in the sea for longer than 5 minutes. Random thoughts that keep me up at night are, “what if I fail at college?” And very often thoughts of my late grandfather. Fun fact about me, I am very dark and morbid. Not depressing or depressed, just dark.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Hey. EponymousRex. Occasionally go by SteelGriffin or Griff sometimes. Long time reader, first time proper official poster. Heh, fiddled around with discussion the old IRC a fair number of years ago. Wanted to write someone/something as a comical doom magnet. Some poor dude attracting suffering enough to make him hate his pitiful existence, but never enough to end it. As if that hasn't been done to death, and honestly I'm surprised I remember it. Oh well.

I might try to do something more than read and so on, but probably not for awhile. Not until I'm over my anxiety and general cowardice.

I always found the Idea beyond the SCP setting, and the general mechanics of it as a collectively written universe to be fascinating. A massive cooperative writing project that has produced something so wonderful and thought provoking, not to mention Fun. So not only am I here for the stories, I'm here to watch the community, and I'm kicking myself for not deciding to become involved sooner.

Anyway to answer the question prompt. Despite my previous noting on my own anxieties, that rarely keeps me up that much. It's more just… My mind gets going on some idea, some story, some THING I want to write, create, etc. Though I do worry. About Family, about the future, all that crap. You know how it is.

Hello everyone, I am very grateful to be a part of this site. I first discovered SCP when I saw a new uploaded video on Youtube at the time SCP-087 in very early 2012. I downloaded the game and played it, I also did a Google search that led me to the article and wow, this website has come a long way and I have finally made the effort to officially join after almost 9 years. I hope you are all doing well!

I am an avid reader and do plan to stay that way for quite some time but I have had some personal suggestions for SCPs but I haven't put the plans into action.

My hobbies are listening to music, watching anime, and playing video games.

As for the question, my answer is: Embarrassing things I did when I was a kid.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Jabobai! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It's great to see you are as fascinated with the SCP Universe as we are here on-site. Hopefully your future readings won't disappoint you and will only make the feeling of wonder even greater. It also seems like you really want to contribute to the site, which I am very happy for; I can't wait to see what you come up with!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!
